newsitem.title: UK: European shares mostly firm as Wall St nerves calm.
newsitem.headline: European shares mostly firm as Wall St nerves calm.

text.p: European shares mostly edged higher in nervous trade on Thursday after Wednesday's hefty losses on Wall Street, with prices underpinned by steady bond markets, dealers said.
Britain's FTSE 100 index, which dropped 53 points on Wednesday, maintained an early firm tone in thin volume by midmorning as investors awaited a lead from Wall Street.
Many institutions remained wary of further losses in New York after the 71-point slide on Wednesday, although there were signs that the Dow Jones index could come in firmer.
"The Dow was down 130 points at one stage last night but did cut its losses which has led some to believe it will rally today," one senior dealer said.
"We've seen the Dow come back before and it may well do it again. But it is still looking overbought and due for a correction," he said.
Dealers noted that the March S&P 500 futures contract on the Globex after-hours trading system was up around 2.00 points, indicating a firmer start for Wall Street.

"We've taken a bit of heart from the S&P's. It looks like we'll have a better day on Wall Street," another trader said. "But if the Dow comes off again, our market tends to panic a bit and follow it lower."
The FTSE 100 was hovering around the 4,000 resistance level by midmorning, up 21.9 points at 4,004.4 after opening 5.3 points higher at 3,987.0.

German shares also shrugged off Wall Street's weakness on Wednesday and climbed in early Frankfurt trading, helped by the strong dollar, although traders were not certain the gains would last through the session.
Dealers said the German 30-share IBIS DAX index may trade in a range between 2,820 and 2,860 points on Thursday. It was up 3.96 points at 2,845.01 by 0932 GMT.
French stocks opened only slightly higher, confounding expectations for a big rebound following the previous day's sharp fall, after the dollar and bonds eased from their early highs, brokers said.
